critical_code_review_comments: notifications.notify(): when target_type and target_id are both None, idempotency uses (kind, subtitle, last-24h) which relies on stable subtitle string; if a source ever changes wording it could re-fire — acceptable for now but worth documenting.

notifications.refresh_notifications(): _LAST_REFRESH is a module-global dict, not per-user; fine since 'global' is the only key used, but the type hint Dict[str, datetime] is a bit misleading — could rename to _LAST_REFRESH_AT.

admin_router.list_notifications(): the refresh_notifications(db) call is awaited on EVERY /admin/notifications request (guarded by TTL 60s). Under high frontend polling (45s interval per open tab × N admins) it will re-scan sources ~every request-that-crosses-60s. Consider running refresh as a background task instead of inline await to avoid latency spikes when TTL just expired.

admin_router.mark_notification_read/dismiss: return 404 if user's required_perm doesn't match — good — but the query `required_perm: {$in: list(_user_perms(user))}` will also 404 for a notification that exists but is out of scope; the error message 'Notificación no encontrada' is slightly misleading for a permission mismatch (would be nice to distinguish 403 vs 404).

NotificationsBell.jsx: dismiss button has class opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 — works visually but is always focusable via keyboard (accessibility could be improved with aria-hidden until hover/focus).
NotificationsBell.jsx polling of 45s per mounted instance — if the admin opens multiple admin tabs, load fires per-tab. Not critical but visible on network panel.
